plate_findings.evidence: Caption: DWI (top) and ADC (bottom) show acute diffusion restriction (yellow arrows) consistent with a new left-paramedial midbrain infarct; in-text: 'acute or chronic small vessel ischemic infarcts (Figure 4)'

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial DWI/ADC MRI from a 3-year-11-month-old boy with DADA2 showing acute diffusion restriction in the left-paramedial midbrain, i.e., a deep small-vessel ischemic infarct. The caption explicitly attributes these ischemic strokes to DADA2 (early-onset, recurrent, deep in the brain), and the article is a DADA2 cohort study, so disease attribution is direct. B: Axial T2 MRI from the same 3-year-11-month-old DADA2 patient showing two prior thalamic lacunar infarcts. Recurrent deep small-vessel strokes are a classic DADA2 presentation, and the caption explicitly ties these strokes to DADA2 in a DADA2 cohort article.
panels.attribution_text: Barron et al. The Spectrum of the Deficiency of Adenosine Deaminase 2: An Observational Analysis of a 60 Patient Cohort.. Frontiers in immunology 2021. doi:10.3389/fimmu.2021.811473. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: The ischemic strokes in DADA2 may present at an early age and can occur, repeatedly, deep in the brain. (A) Shows the diffusion weighted imaging (DWI) (top) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) (bottom) indicative of acute diffusion restriction (yellow arrows) consistent with a new left-paramedial midbrain infarct. (B) The same study, on T2 images a few cuts above, shows evidence of two prior lacunar strokes on the thalamus (blue arrows). These strokes occurred in a 3 year 11-month-old boy.

Hemorrhagic strokes were observed in 7 patients ( Figure 5 ), with 6 of the 7 also demonstrating prior ischemic strokes. One patient presented with a large hemorrhagic stroke, without a history of ischemic strokes. plate_findings.evidence: Sections of skin biopsy showing lymphovascular occlusion in medium vessels in the medium-to-deep dermis with inflammatory infiltrate with neutrophils and intravascular thrombi

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: H&E skin biopsy from a DADA2 patient (per figure caption and DADA2 cohort article) showing medium-vessel lymphovascular occlusion with neutrophilic infiltrate and intravascular thrombi, matching the configured necrotizing small- to medium-vessel vasculitis finding. Arrows annotate affected vessels. B: H&E section of a medium-sized artery from a DADA2 patient (caption: vasculitis in DADA2 patients resembling polyarteritis nodosa) with dense transmural mononuclear and neutrophilic infiltrate, karyorrhexis, luminal fibrin and vessel wall destruction — necrotizing medium-vessel vasculitis per the configured vocabulary. C: H&E section showing vasculitis of smaller vessels in the superficial subcutis; the biopsy was morphologically interpreted as possible polyarteritis nodosa, but the figure caption and DADA2 cohort article frame it as vasculitis in DADA2 patients (DADA2 vasculitis classically mimics PAN), so the panel is attributed to DADA2...
panels.attribution_text: Barron et al. The Spectrum of the Deficiency of Adenosine Deaminase 2: An Observational Analysis of a 60 Patient Cohort.. Frontiers in immunology 2021. doi:10.3389/fimmu.2021.811473. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: The medium vessel vasculitis in DADA2 patients resembles the vasculitis in polyarteritis nodosa. (A) Sections of skin biopsy showing lymphovascular occlusion in medium vessels in the medium-to-deep dermis with inflammatory infiltrate with neutrophils and intravascular thrombi. (B) Vasculitis of a medium sized artery characterized by dense transmural infiltrate of mononuclear cells and neutrophils with karyorrhexis, fibrin deposits in vascular lumen, destruction of vessel walls and dense chronic inflammation surrounding the affected blood vessel. (C) Vasculitis involving smaller blood vessels of the superficial subcutis. This biopsy was interpreted as possible polyarteritis nodosa.
in_text_mentions: g underlying immune deficiency (14). There was a range of skin biopsy findings including lesions showing lymphovascular occlusion in medium vessels with inflammatory infiltrates and intravascular thrombi ( Figure 3A ). Vasculitis of medium-sized arterial vessels that resembled PAN was noted with features of mononuclear cells and neutrophils, karyorrhexis, fibrin deposits in vascular lumens, destruction of vessel walls, and dense chronic inflammation surrounding affected blood vessels ( Figure 3B ). Vasculitis involving smaller blood vessels of the superficial cutis was also seen ( Figure 3C ).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Clinical photograph of a lower leg/ankle showing a well-defined irregular ulceration with yellow fibrinous exudate (black arrow). The figure is explicitly titled 'Skin ulceration in DADA2' in a DADA2 cohort article, and the caption attributes the ulcer to DADA2 in a 40-year-old patient; the passing mention of adalimumab use does not change disease attribution. Ulceration is a named manifestation but has no vocabulary key, so it is recorded as a proposed finding. B: Clinical photograph of the foot/ankle distal to the knees showing mottled reticular erythema that the caption explicitly identifies as livedo racemosa, a classic and vocabulary-supported DADA2 cutaneous manifestation. Disease attribution is direct from the caption within a DADA2 cohort article. C: Clinical photograph of the lower legs showing multiple hypopigmented atrophic plaques that the caption states are scars from prior ulcerations (white arrows), i.e. sequelae of...
panels.attribution_text: Barron et al. The Spectrum of the Deficiency of Adenosine Deaminase 2: An Observational Analysis of a 60 Patient Cohort.. Frontiers in immunology 2021. doi:10.3389/fimmu.2021.811473. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 10.
panels.figure_caption: Skin ulceration in DADA2. (A) A 40-year-old developed a well-defined, irregularly shaped ulceration with overlying yellow fibrinous exudate (black arrow). The ulcer was not infected. There had been antecedent trauma 3 months prior with a small skin tear. This lesion developed while on adalimumab and screening for neutralizing antibodies to adalimumab was negative. (B) Distal to the knees there was increasing mottled, somewhat reticular erythema representing livedo racemosa. (C) Further examination revealed multiple hypopigmented atrophic plaques consistent with scars from prior ulcerations (white arrows).
in_text_mentions: • 39-year-old female (Patient 45) with a history of multiple chronic ankle ulcerations ( Figure 10 ) and Raynaud’s phenomenon. Lower DBI waveform and pressure was abnormal in her digits, suggesting small-vessel disease. MRA revealed attenuated appearance of the peroneal artery.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Clinical photograph of both legs showing livedo racemosa in a 38-year-old from a DADA2 cohort; the in-text states livedo racemosa was present in 43/58 patients (74%) (Figure 2A). This is the classic, most frequent cutaneous manifestation of DADA2, directly attributed by the disease-focused article and panel-specific caption. B: Clinical photograph of the lower leg/ankle showing subcutaneous nodules in a 58-year-old; the panel-specific caption states the nodules, when biopsied, revealed medium-vessel vasculitis (cutaneous PAN). The in-text reports PAN-like cutaneous nodules in 33/58 patients (57%) (Figure 2B). The visible nodules and the caption-stated biopsy-proven medium-vessel vasculitis are both classic DADA2 manifestations. panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph showing reticulate reddish-violaceous skin discoloration on a lower limb, consistent with livedo racemosa. The article is focused on DADA2 (testicular ischemia in DADA2), and the caption and in-text mention explicitly attribute this livedo racemosa to the patient with DADA2. Livedo racemosa is a recognized classic cutaneous manifestation of DADA2. The image is a real patient clinical photograph with adequate quality and no third-party copyright indicated.

panels.rationale: H&E photomicrograph of a testicular biopsy from a DADA2 patient (article title: 'Testicular ischemia in deficiency of adenosine deaminase 2'). The panel visibly shows patchy tubular necrosis with loss of cellular/nuclear detail and nuclear smudging alongside viable tubules, i.e., the ischemic manifestation of DADA2. In-text evidence links the hemorrhage and acute inflammatory cells to an underlying vasculitic process, supporting the necrotizing vasculitis finding key. Tubular necrosis/testicular ischemia is not in the vocabulary and is listed as proposed findings. Testicular ischemia is a recognized but less common DADA2 manifestation, so typicality is variant.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: H&E section of the left lower leg ulcer biopsy from the ADA2-deficiency case report; the panel shows a medium-sized vessel with intimal wall thickening, fibrosis and an occlusive thrombus, a recognized vasculitic pattern of ADA2 deficiency (vocabulary finding: necrotizing small/medium-vessel vasculitis). b: H&E section at 20× explicitly captioned as small-vessel vasculitis with perivascular inflammatory infiltrates; attributed to ADA2 deficiency per the disease-focused article title and the vocabulary finding. c: H&E section at 20× showing interstitial neutrophilic and eosinophilic infiltrate with fibrosis, the inflammatory component of the vasculitis biopsy; attributed to ADA2 deficiency per the article title.
